C-METADATA-SAVE-SAFETY.Summary: Preserve unsaved document text and the selected file format across metadata changes, Save, Save All and save-before-close. The owner's active stabilization goal selects end-to-end format ownership (option B); approval of this exact spec and its later implementation plan remains separate.

Problem.Baseline: Investigation baseline: 94db8add579d3a2354c2d2cb9eb0e7a90cce759b, after the Save/Close and link repairs. Those candidates remain subject to their separate acceptance and integration decisions. Implementation must revalidate the eventual accepted baseline.
Problem.Evidence: Existing metadata characterizations reproduce a dirty tab marked clean and closed without a prompt after a format change. A private built-renderer matrix additionally observes encoding, EOL and final-newline changes while Save and Save and Close are pending: format changes do not advance the snapshot revision, old acknowledgements become clean, and close proceeds without persisting the newer format. This is renderer evidence with backend doubles. Source inspection shows format fields absent from documentSnapshot, DocumentWriteRequest and the Rust writer, while build_open_new_tab_payload supplies fixed UTF-8/LF metadata. The existing encoding crate needs an explicit alias/capability catalog; direct UI IDs cannot be assumed to be backend labels.

Goals.R-001: Any effective change to a document's encoding, BOM policy, EOL policy or final-newline policy is an unsaved document change. It must never mark existing unsaved text clean. Preserve the exact committed Markdown, editing surface, selection and history when changing a format choice. Re-selecting the current effective value is a no-op and preserves dirty state and revision.
Goals.R-002: Save freshness covers the owned document lifetime, text and selected format together. A format change during a picker, confirmation or write cannot be ignored because the text is unchanged. Acknowledgement of an older format cannot mark a newer choice saved or close the document. Keep the newer state open and unsaved with the existing explicit-retry feedback pattern; do not silently resave or resume closure.
Goals.R-003: Save, Save As, Save All, autosave and save-before-close use one immutable text-and-format snapshot and matching result contract. A metadata-only dirty document participates even if Markdown did not change. Only a matching successful write of the requested version may establish its saved checkpoint. Cancellation or failure preserves the buffer, format choices, dirty state and existing Save/Close batch barrier.
Goals.R-004: Apply EOL and final-newline transformations at the write boundary without rewriting the live canonical model. LF/CRLF output is deterministic and never creates doubled carriage returns. Final-newline options mean remove trailing line breaks, ensure exactly one final line break, or leave the canonical trailing breaks unchanged. A selected EOL policy then applies to all output line breaks.
Goals.R-005: For declared supported output codecs, bytes must represent the selected encoding and BOM policy exactly. Validate codec, policy and representability and construct the complete bytes before opening a destination for mutation. Unsupported codecs, invalid policies or unrepresentable characters fail visibly before truncating or writing the target. No implicit UTF-8 fallback, replacement characters, question-mark substitution or HTML entity conversion may count as a successful save.
Goals.R-006: Use an explicit audited catalog mapping every advertised UI encoding ID and visible meaning to a supported backend codec or an explicit unavailable state. A visible choice must not claim working support when the writer cannot provide it. Existing UI identifiers may be normalized internally, with coherent types and replies. UTF-16 output must not silently use the encoding crate's UTF-8 encoder. The exact catalog and treatment of unavailable choices are owner-review inputs before plan approval.
Goals.R-007: Normal document opening must propagate actual detected encoding, BOM and EOL metadata needed for supported writeback instead of fixed UTF-8/LF defaults. Retain the existing opening routes, canonical duplicate-tab reuse and access checks. The default disabled normalization policy preserves the supported source format; explicit EOL/final-newline choices request conversion on the next save. Mixed-EOL input is identified and never silently normalized. Without an explicit supported write policy, refuse byte-changing save visibly and require a LF/CRLF choice rather than inventing per-line preservation. New untitled documents use the existing applicable defaults.
Goals.R-008: Format-dirty state survives tab switching, rich/source/split switching, text undo/redo, history restoration and session restoration. Undoing text to a saved text checkpoint cannot clear an outstanding format change. Existing dirty target reuse retains its live format state. Normal caret navigation, hover and unchanged metadata do not dirty a saved document.
Goals.R-009: Preserve active IME protection, complete-model serialization including unmounted tails, fresh explicit retries, owned-path collision rejection and document-lifetime isolation. Selecting a format cannot destroy preedit or force a renderer import. Any format UI action unsafe during composition must refuse with existing nonmodal feedback rather than synthesize composition completion.
Goals.R-010: Keep security fences, bookmark/capability access, text history, table/Find/link interactions, localization and existing test/performance floors. Do not make byte-policy errors look like a completed save. Distinguish byte-identity evidence from browser transport doubles and owner acceptance from automated verification.

Constraints.Constraint: The active stabilization goal selects option B and authorizes preparation of its exact spec and implementation plan. This spec remains draft until approved; product implementation follows approval of the completed plan. The goal separately authorizes integration of the preceding Save/Close, link and timestamp repairs. Current accepted test artifacts stay unchanged. Version changes, release dispatch and publication remain unauthorized.

Use one sequential bounded change and the existing document operation coordinator. Select the complete approach after owner review. An implementation plan follows approved spec scope; it must pin the actual codec catalog, write and read consumers, format checkpoints and evidence commands without carrying investigative history into the normative body.

Graph, verification, module contracts, DTO types, backend validation and live tests must describe the same approved format contract. Preserve frozen archives. Repaired characterizations must assert the new invariant; unrelated historical defect observations remain truthful. Do not weaken retries, timeouts, skips, coverage or performance budgets.

All byte construction failures must precede filesystem mutation. General I/O failure atomicity and crash durability remain separate: this item must not claim them merely because encoding validation is safe.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Rename/Move To UI repair; global physical-write scheduling; atomic replace, crash recovery or WAL; external-change byte-equivalence redesign; new multi-window behavior; richer encoding-detection heuristics or a new manual re-decode interface.

Automatic support for every historical encoding name without a proven mapping, arbitrary plugin codecs, export/theme/agent features, release preparation or publication, and owner acceptance on behalf of the owner.

AcceptanceCriteria.AC-001: Named and untitled rich/source/split documents cover all format setters: clean and dirty text, no-op selection, later typing, undo/redo and tab switches. No format setter clears unsaved text or rewrites canonical Markdown/history. Unsupported or composition-unsafe actions give a visible safe outcome.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-002: Controlled delayed Save, Save As and Save and Close cases change each owned format field after dispatch and during picker/confirmation. Older acknowledgements cannot establish the newer saved checkpoint or close it. Explicit retry writes the fresh selected format and closes only after a matching acknowledgement; batch cancellation/failure closes no target.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-003: Backend byte fixtures establish exact UTF-8 with/without BOM, supported UTF-16 endianness/BOM, LF/CRLF, empty text and the three final-newline policies, plus a representable non-UTF fixture from the approved catalog. Invalid labels/policies and unrepresentable text leave an existing sentinel file byte-identical. Every UI entry has a tested catalog disposition; no fallback is labelled support.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-004: Actual native open/save/reopen evidence uses supported BOM/EOL/non-UTF fixtures and verifies selected metadata and bytes. Existing dirty-tab reuse retains format state; fresh open uses detected metadata. Mixed-EOL fixtures prove absence of silent normalization and a safe outcome until an explicit supported policy is selected. Browser doubles do not stand in for this evidence.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-005: Save All handles metadata-only changes and all existing loss-prevention cases without lost Markdown or premature closure. Focused coordinator, snapshot, store, transport and backend tests cover stale lifetimes/paths, format freshness, encoding failures and ordinary undo/caret behavior. Existing accepted interactions and complete-model large-document checks remain green.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-006: The exact approved implementation candidate passes full renderer coverage, IPC typecheck, renderer build, backend tests, selected browser tiers, required hosted gates and deterministic commit/push checks. One isolated attributed QA artifact has a short format-state/bytes acceptance checklist. Owner verdict and apply/archive remain separate.

AffectedAreas.Paths: Renderer document state/setters, snapshot/coordinator and content/history dirty reconciliation; file-format commands/defaults and save DTOs/transports; native correlated writer, encoding helper and document-open metadata adapters; owned tests, graph and verification entries. The later approved plan fixes exact write scope.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Red/green desired-invariant cases derived from the observed false-clean, silent-close and in-flight metadata families; immutable text/format/revision traces; deterministic exact-byte fixtures and pre-write failure sentinels; supported/unavailable codec catalog; source-bound native evidence distinct from renderer observations.
Focused tests and browser/native protocols are selected in the approved plan. No new speculative implementation test suite or production change belongs to this drafting stage.

Assumptions.OwnerDecision: The owner's active stabilization goal selects option B: one coherent format-snapshot/read/write item, rather than only removing the three false-clean assignments. A guard-only implementation does not satisfy the goal.
Assumptions.ProposedDefault: Unsupported choices are unavailable with a clear explanation; unrepresentable content refuses saving without target mutation. No automatic switch to UTF-8. The supported codec catalog and unavailable-choice presentation need owner confirmation.

Format changes during an outstanding save follow the owner's existing text-change policy: retain the newer unsaved state and require an explicit fresh retry. This application to metadata is proposed, not a new recorded owner decision.
Assumptions.OpenDecision: The exact spec and later completed plan, including the audited codec catalog and unavailable-choice treatment, still require approval. Scope selection does not itself approve an unreviewed plan.
